'''Joseph Steven Crispin''' (born July 18, 1979) is an American men's [[college basketball]] coach and former player. He is currently the head coach of the [[Air Force Falcons men's basketball]] team. He previously served as an assistant coach at [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State University]] and as the head coach at [[Rowan Profs men's basketball|Rowan University]].

==Early life==
Crispin was born at [[Underwood-Memorial Hospital]] in [[Woodbury, New Jersey]].<ref>{{cite news|url = https://www.newspapers.com/image/1105064364/|title = Births; Underwood-Memorial|date = August 7, 1979|newspaper = [[Gloucester County Times]]|page = 9|via = [[Newspapers.com]]|url-access = subscription|accessdate = December 6, 2024}}</ref>

He later starred as a [[point guard]] for [[Pitman High School]], leading the Panthers to the New Jersey Group I state championship in 1997 while setting the [[Gloucester County, New Jersey|Gloucester County]] all-time scoring record for boys' high school basketball. He averaged 35.6 points per game during his junior and senior seasons, and 24.9 points per game across his entire high school career. Across 117 career games, he failed to score at least 10 points only once.{{cn|date=March 2026}}

==College career==
Crispin played [[college basketball]] at [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]] alongside his brother, [[Jon Crispin]].<ref>[http://www.bigbluehistory.net/bb/statistics/Games/20001125PennState.html Penn State at Kentucky – November 25, 2000], by Stephen John; Kentucky Sports Report</ref> The brothers were part of the [[2000-01 Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball team|2001 Penn State team]] that upset national powerhouse [[2000-01 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the [[2001 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]].{{cn|date=March 2026}}

==Professional career==
===NBA career===
Crispin played in the [[NBA]] during the [[2001-02 NBA season|2001-02 season]], splitting time between the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] and [[Phoenix Suns]]. He signed with the [[Miami Heat]] in 2003<ref>[http://www.insidehoops.com/heat-sign-092903.shtml Heat sign Ike Austin and Joe Crispin], September 29, 2003</ref> but was waived before the [[2003-04 NBA season|2003–04 season]] began.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat_waives_crispin_031014.html HEAT Request Waivers on Joe Crispin], October 14, 2003</ref><ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.psu.edu/sports/basketball/men/profiles/Joe.Crispin.html |title=Joe Crispin |access-date=March 24, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20050322070902/http://www.psu.edu/sports/basketball/men/profiles/Joe.Crispin.html |archive-date=March 22, 2005 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Overseas career===
Crispin has also played in the [[American Basketball Association (2000-)|ABA]], [[Continental Basketball Association|CBA]], [[United States Basketball League|USBL]], with [[Anwil Włocławek]] of the [[Dominet Bank Ekstraliga|Polish Basketball League]],<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.24sec.net/article.asp?index=2142 |title=24sec.net – Basketball News – Joe Crispin in Teramo<!-- Bot generated title --> |access-date=March 24, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20061012071529/http://www.24sec.net/article.asp?index=2142 |archive-date=October 12, 2006 |url-status=dead }}</ref> with [[Teramo Basket|Teramo]] in Italy,<ref>[http://www.hoopshype.com/players/joseph_crispin.htm HoopsHype – NBA Players – Joseph Crispin]</ref> and with [[Bandırma Banvit|Banvit]] of the [[Turkish Basketball League]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/team.asp?Cntry=tur&Team=4718 EuroBasket]</ref> He signed with Barcellona Pozzo di Gotto in Italy for the 2010–11 season. The next season, he joined [[Azovmash Mariupol]] in [[Ukraine]].<ref>[http://www.eurobasket.com/player.asp?Cntry=ITA&PlayerID=31824 Joe Crispin]. Eurobasket.</ref>

==Coaching career==
On March 18, 2026, Crispin was announced as the next head men's basketball coach at the [[Air Force Falcons men's basketball|United States Air Force Academy]]. He had previously spent several years as the head coach at [[Rowan University]] and as an assistant coach at [[Penn State Nittany Lions men's basketball|Penn State]].<ref>{{cite web| url=https://krdo.com/news/sports-news/2026/03/18/air-force-hires-joe-crispin-as-new-head-coach-of-mens-basketball/| title=Air Force Hires Joe Crispin as New Head Coach of Men's Basketball| website=krdo.com| first=Dylan| last=Foreman| date=March 18, 2026| access-date=March 30, 2026}}</ref>
